newsitem.title: USA: Oklahoma sorghum harvest progresses rapidly.
newsitem.headline: Oklahoma sorghum harvest progresses rapidly.

text.p: Harvesting of Oklahoma's grain sorghum crop made good progress as dry weather held over the western part of the state during the week ended Sunday, according to the weekly state crop report.
Meanwhile, field activities were slowed as rains fell in the central and eastern areas of the state. Moisture was needed in western areas for crop development and germination of late-planted wheat.
Wheat emerged was rated at 91 percent, compared to 85 a week ago, 76 a year ago and 79 percent on a five-year average.
Wheat rated 83 percent good to excellent, vs 81 at that level last week.
Sorghum harvested 69 percent vs 34 w/a, 68 y/a, 68 avg.
Soybeans harvested 81 percent vs 62 w/a, 73 y/a, 69 avg.
Cotton bolls opening 87 percent vs 84 w/a, 86 y/a, 89 avg.
Cotton harvested 28 percent vs 24 w/a, 23 y/a, 4 avg.
Cotton rated 30 percent good/excellent, vs 33 last week.
Pasture and range condition rated 74 percent good to excellent vs 73 last week.
